units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And if I have more than a day?

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Or I'm sick of cobblestones?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then go and look at three other Brussels.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The first is Art Nouveau.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Curves and flowers.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In the eighteen-nineties, a young architect named Victor Horta built a townhouse for a professor called Emile Tassel.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Iron columns shaped like plant stems, stairs that curl like vines, and light pouring down from above.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1893 and 1894. It's widely regarded as the first Art Nouveau building.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And there's a museum.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Horta Museum, in Saint-Gilles, in the house where he lived and worked.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Several of his houses are now UNESCO World Heritage.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: If you want just one museum, I'd pick that.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What's the second Brussels?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Comics.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Tintin!

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A young Brussels cartoonist named Georges Remi, who signed his work Hergé, published the first adventure of a young reporter with a quiff of red hair, in a children's supplement, in January of 1929.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That quiff is iconic.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And Belgium's comic strip tradition has made Brussels a world capital of the form.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You'll find big comic murals on the sides of buildings around the center, if you keep your eyes up.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Eyes up. Got it. And the third?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The European quarter. Take the metro to Schuman station and walk out.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You'll face the Berlaymont, the star-shaped headquarters of the European Commission.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: It's not exactly cute.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's not charming in the way the Grand Place is.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: But it tells you what the city is for now.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A slightly different kind of landmark.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A different kind, and every bit as much part of the story.
